lessons.title: Monohybrid inheritance
lessons.programRef: GCE O Level Biology — Inheritance: genes, alleles, dominance, monohybrid crosses, test cross (to be checked against the official syllabus)
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original text written for the GCE O Level Biology syllabus; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Use the terms gene, allele, dominant, recessive, homozygous, heterozygous, genotype and phenotype correctly.
Set out a monohybrid cross with a genetic diagram and a Punnett square.
Explain the 3 : 1 and 1 : 1 ratios and use a test cross.

blocks.title: Genes and alleles
blocks.md:
- A **gene** is a length of DNA on a chromosome that controls a characteristic (for example, stem height in peas).
- **Alleles** are different forms of the same gene (for example, "tall" T and "short" t).
- Body cells have chromosomes in pairs, so each individual carries **two alleles** of each gene. A gamete carries only **one**.

blocks.title: Dominant and recessive
blocks.md:
- A **dominant** allele (capital letter, T) shows its effect even when only one copy is present.
- A **recessive** allele (small letter, t) shows its effect only when two copies are present (tt).
- **Homozygous**: two identical alleles (TT or tt). **Heterozygous**: two different alleles (Tt).

blocks.title: Genotype and phenotype
blocks.md:
- The **genotype** is the pair of alleles an organism has: TT, Tt or tt.
- The **phenotype** is the observable characteristic: tall or short.

TT and Tt give the same phenotype (tall) because T is dominant. Only tt gives short plants.

blocks.title: Method: setting out a monohybrid cross
blocks.md:
1. Choose a letter: capital for the dominant allele, the same small letter for the recessive one.
2. Write the parents' phenotypes and genotypes.
3. Write the gametes: each gamete receives **one** allele.
4. Combine the gametes in a **Punnett square**.
5. List the offspring genotypes and their ratio.
6. Give the offspring phenotypes and their ratio.

blocks.caption: Punnett square for Tt × Tt: 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt, so 3 tall : 1 short.
blocks.alt: A two-by-two grid. The columns are headed by the male gametes T and t, the rows by the female gametes T and t. The boxes contain TT, Tt, Tt (green, tall) and tt (yellow, short).

blocks.title: The two ratios to know
blocks.md:
- **Tt × Tt** (two heterozygotes): genotypes 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt; phenotypes **3 dominant : 1 recessive** (75 % : 25 %).
- **Tt × tt** (heterozygote × homozygous recessive): genotypes 1 Tt : 1 tt; phenotypes **1 : 1** (50 % : 50 %).

These ratios are **probabilities**: real numbers of offspring are only close to them, and closer when there are many offspring.

blocks.title: The test cross
blocks.md:
A tall plant can be TT or Tt: they look the same. To find out, cross it with a **homozygous recessive** plant (tt).

- All offspring tall → the unknown parent is **TT**.
- About half tall, half short (1 : 1) → the unknown parent is **Tt**.

blocks.title: Worked example 1: pure-breeding parents, then the F2
blocks.statement: In pea plants, tall (T) is dominant to short (t). A pure-breeding tall plant is crossed with a short plant. The F1 plants are then self-pollinated. Give the F1 and F2 phenotypes and ratio.

steps.md: "Pure-breeding" means homozygous. Parents: tall **TT** × short **tt** (short must be tt because t is recessive).
Gametes: the tall parent gives only **T**, the short parent only **t**. Every F1 plant is **Tt**, so every F1 plant is **tall**.
F1 self-pollinated: Tt × Tt. Gametes T or t from each parent. The Punnett square gives 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt.
TT and Tt are tall, tt is short: F2 phenotypes **3 tall : 1 short**. The short character, hidden in F1, reappears in F2.

blocks.title: Worked example 2: working back from data
blocks.statement: Two plants with purple flowers are crossed. The offspring are 612 purple-flowered and 212 white-flowered plants. Which allele is dominant, and what are the genotypes of the parents? (Use P and p.)

steps.md: Two purple parents give some white offspring: white was hidden in the parents, so **white is recessive** and **purple (P) is dominant**.
Calculate the ratio: 612 ÷ 212 ≈ 2.9, so about **3 purple : 1 white**.
A 3 : 1 ratio comes from a cross between two heterozygotes. The white offspring are pp: they received one p from **each** parent.
So both parents carry p while being purple: both are **Pp**.

blocks.answer: **Purple is dominant; both parents are heterozygous, Pp × Pp.**

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.md:
- Confusing **gene** (the characteristic) and **allele** (a version of it).
- Putting two alleles in a gamete: a gamete has **one**.
- Using different letters, such as T and s: use one letter, capital and small (T and t).
- Thinking a 3 : 1 ratio means exactly 3 of 4 offspring: it is a probability.
- Believing a dominant allele is always the most common one in a population.

items: Gregor Mendel discovered these rules in the 1860s by crossing thousands of pea plants and counting the offspring.
Some alleles are neither dominant nor recessive (codominance): for example, the ABO blood groups in humans. This is studied separately.

reviewNotes: Check the notation expected by the Cameroon GCE Board for genetic diagrams (for example, circles around gametes, use of 'F1' and 'F2').

exercises.prompt: What is meant by the phenotype of an organism?
choices: The pair of alleles it carries
exercises.explanation: The phenotype is what can be observed (tall, short, purple...). The pair of alleles is the genotype.
mistakes: Swapping the definitions of genotype and phenotype.
exercises.source: Original exercise, GCE O Level style

exercises.prompt: Match each term with its meaning.
pairs: Shows its effect only when two copies are present
exercises.explanation: Allele: version of a gene. Homozygous: TT or tt. Heterozygous: Tt. Recessive: expressed only in tt. Genotype: the combination of alleles.
exercises.source: Original exercise, GCE O Level style

exercises.prompt: A heterozygous tall pea plant (Tt) is crossed with a short plant (tt). What percentage of the offspring are expected to be short?
exercises.explanation: Gametes: T or t from the first parent, only t from the second. Offspring: 1 Tt : 1 tt, so 50 % short (tt).
exercises.method: Draw the Punnett square: 2 of the 4 boxes are tt.
mistakes: Answering 25 %: that is for Tt × Tt.
exercises.source: Original exercise, GCE O Level style

exercises.prompt: Two heterozygous tall pea plants (Tt × Tt) produce 360 seeds, all of which grow. How many short plants are expected?
exercises.explanation: Tt × Tt gives 3 tall : 1 short, so 1 plant in 4 is short: 360 ÷ 4 = 90 short plants (and 270 tall).
exercises.method: Convert the ratio into a fraction of the total: 1 : 3 means 1/4 short.
mistakes: Dividing by 3 instead of 4 (the ratio 3 : 1 has 4 parts).
exercises.source: Original exercise, GCE O Level style

exercises.prompt: A black guinea pig (black B is dominant to white b) is crossed with a white guinea pig. They have 10 offspring: 5 black and 5 white. What is the genotype of the black parent?
choices: It cannot be determined from these results
exercises.explanation: The white parent is bb and gives only b. White offspring (bb) must have received b from the black parent too, so it is Bb. Bb × bb gives the observed 1 : 1 ratio.
exercises.method: This is a test cross: any recessive offspring shows that the dominant parent is heterozygous.
exercises.source: Original exercise, GCE O Level style

exercises.prompt: In maize, purple grain colour (P) is dominant to yellow grain colour (p). A farmer in the West Region crosses two maize plants that are both heterozygous for grain colour.
exercises.method: Write the genetic diagram (parents, gametes, Punnett square, offspring) before answering.
mistakes: Giving the ratio 1 : 2 : 1 when the question asks about phenotypes.
exercises.source: Original exercise, GCE O Level style

parts.prompt: What is the genotype of each parent plant?
parts.explanation: Heterozygous means two different alleles: Pp.

parts.prompt: Which gametes can each parent produce?
choices: Half carry P and half carry p
Every gamete carries the dominant allele
Every gamete carries the recessive allele
parts.explanation: Each gamete receives one allele: half the gametes carry P, half carry p.

parts.prompt: What percentage of the grains are expected to be yellow?
parts.explanation: Pp × Pp gives 1 PP : 2 Pp : 1 pp. Only pp is yellow: 1 in 4, or 25 %.

parts.prompt: A cob from this cross carries 480 grains. How many purple grains are expected?
parts.explanation: Purple = 3/4 of the grains: 480 × 3 ÷ 4 = 360 purple grains (and 120 yellow).

parts.prompt: The farmer wants to know whether a purple-grained plant is PP or Pp. Describe a cross that would tell him, and how to interpret the results.
parts.model: Cross the purple plant with a yellow plant (pp): a test cross (1 mark). If all the grains are purple, the plant is PP; if about half are yellow (1 : 1), it is Pp (1 mark).
rubric: 1 mark: cross with a homozygous recessive (yellow, pp) plant.
1 mark: correct interpretation of both possible results.
parts.explanation: Only a homozygous recessive partner reveals the hidden allele: any yellow grain proves that the purple parent carries p.

choices: Different forms of the same gene
Two different genes on one chromosome
exercises.explanation: Alleles are alternative forms of one gene, such as T (tall) and t (short).

choices: Tt: one tall and one short allele
exercises.explanation: Heterozygous means two different alleles: Tt. TT and tt are homozygous; T alone is a gamete.

exercises.prompt: What phenotype ratio is expected from the cross Tt × Tt (T dominant)?
exercises.explanation: Genotypes 1 TT : 2 Tt : 1 tt give 3 dominant : 1 recessive phenotypes. 1 : 2 : 1 is the genotype ratio.

exercises.prompt: How many alleles of each gene does a gamete carry?
exercises.explanation: Gametes are formed by meiosis and carry one allele of each gene; fertilisation restores the pair.

exercises.prompt: In a test cross, the organism with the dominant phenotype is crossed with...
exercises.explanation: Only a homozygous recessive partner shows whether the dominant parent carries a hidden recessive allele.

exercises.prompt: Question 3 — Genetics (5 marks). In guinea pigs, black coat (B) is dominant to white coat (b). Two black guinea pigs are mated several times and produce some white offspring.
exercises.method: Start from the recessive offspring: their genotype is certain.
exercises.source: Original exercise, GCE O Level style

parts.prompt: What are the genotypes of the two black parents?
parts.explanation: White offspring are bb and received one b from each parent; being black, each parent must be Bb.

parts.prompt: What percentage of the offspring are expected to be white?
parts.explanation: Bb × Bb gives 1 BB : 2 Bb : 1 bb: 1 in 4 is white, 25 %.

parts.prompt: Over several litters the pair has 12 offspring. How many are expected to be black?
Explain how two black parents can have white offspring.
parts.model: Each parent is heterozygous (Bb) and carries the recessive allele b hidden by the dominant B (1 mark). Each parent can pass on a gamete carrying b; if two b gametes fuse, the offspring is bb and white (1 mark).
rubric: 1 mark: parents heterozygous, recessive allele hidden.
1 mark: offspring receives b from each parent, bb = white.
parts.explanation: The recessive allele is masked in the parents but expressed when it is inherited from both.
